title: Eilenberg finiteness: infinite fibres of a Lipschitz map on a finite-Hᵏ Borel set lie over a Lebesgue-null set
statement: Let N, m ∈ ℕ and k := m + 1. Let ℝ^N = Eucl N carry Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized Euclidean k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, and let ℝᵏ = Eucl k carry Lebesgue measure Lᵏ (volume). Let E ⊆ ℝ^N be a Borel set with Hᵏ(E) < ∞. Let f : ℝ^N → ℝᵏ be Lipschitz with constant K ∈ [0, ∞), i.e. |f(x) − f(x′)| ≤ K|x − x′| for all x, x′. Then the set {y ∈ ℝᵏ : E ∩ f⁻¹({y}) is infinite} has Lebesgue measure zero.
lean_statement: ∀ (N m : ℕ) (E : Set (Eucl N)) (f : Eucl N → Eucl (m + 1)) (K : ℝ≥0), MeasurableSet E → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl N)) E < ∞ → LipschitzWith K f → (volume : Measure (Eucl (m + 1))) {y : Eucl (m + 1) | (E ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}).Infinite} = 0
